claims.text: Adding a minor copper fraction to the refractory HEA can produce Cu-rich coherent nanoprecipitates.
Cu-rich coherent nanoprecipitates will improve the effective heat-transfer capability of the HEA intermediate layer.
The proposed Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will improve heat transfer without sacrificing structural integrity under plasma-facing reactor conditions.
Refractory HEAs such as (CrFeTiTa)70W30 have been investigated as intermediate layers between tungsten plasma-facing material and CuCrZr cooling structures.
The baseline HEA has a homogeneous solid-solution microstructure produced by conventional processing.
A stepwise controllable nanoprecipitation process can generate uniformly dispersed, coherent Cu-rich precipitates in the proposed intermediate-layer HEA.
The intervention will remain effective at approximately 800–1200 °C.
The intervention will remain effective under cyclic thermomechanical loading and reactor-relevant irradiation.
Coherent Cu-rich nanoprecipitates will enhance electron and phonon heat conduction.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will resist dislocation motion and thereby improve mechanical stability.
Copper's high intrinsic thermal conductivity will allow Cu-rich precipitates to provide low-resistance heat-transfer paths.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will minimize interfacial thermal scattering.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will reduce stress concentrations and help preserve mechanical integrity.
The modified HEA will have higher effective thermal conductivity, producing a lower temperature gradient at the same applied heat flux.
The modified HEA will maintain or improve mechanical strength relative to the conventional HEA layer.
The modified HEA will maintain or improve resistance to irradiation-induced damage.
The current HEA interlayer meets structural requirements but has suboptimal heat-transfer efficiency across the tungsten–CuCrZr interface.
Excessive copper or processing deviations that produce incoherent second phases could impair mechanical stability.
